newsitem.title: ITALY: Costa shares resume higher after suspension.
newsitem.headline: Costa shares resume higher after suspension.

text.p: Shares in Italian cruise line Costa Crociere resumed trade sharply higher on Thursday after three days of suspension on the Milan bourse pending an announcement of an offer from an Anglo-American partnership.
Costa ordinary shares started trade at 3,700 lire a share from their last quote before suspension on Monday at 3,181 lire, and towards the level of the bid at 3,800 lire.

Earlier on Thursday, the British-based holiday operator Airtours Plc and its U.S. cruise partner Carnival Corp said they had signed a letter of intent with the main owners of Costa Crociere to purchase the group.

The two prospective purchasers said that in due course they expected to launch a join tender offer which would make them 50-50 owners of Costa and they expected to pay about 452 billion lire or 181 million pounds in total.

Costa savings shares started at 2,390 lire from 1,900 lire Monday and compared to the 2,500 lire of the purchase offer. The savings warrants were quoted at 278 lire from 260 lire Monday and 285 lire in the offer.
